1.word_for_word: अष्टपञ्चाशत्तमे तु कृष्णः पञ्च-करे\ऽग्रहीत् । — In the fifty-eighth, Krishna took the five-hand\'s.; कालिन्दीं मित्रविन्दां च सत्यां भद्रां च लक्ष्मणाम् ॥ — I married Kalindi Mitravindha Satya Bhadra and Lakshmana; कालिन्दीं निज-लाभाय तपः परम् उपेयुषीम् । — Kalindi, who had undergone great austerities for her own benefit.; परिणेष्यन् प्रियावासम् इन्द्रप्रस्थम् अथागमत् ॥ — After marrying his beloved wife, he returned to Indraprastha.; प्रतीतान् नष्टान् अपि द्रुपद-गृहे पुनः सर्वैर् दृष्टान् । — Everyone saw them again in the house of Drupada even though they had appeared to be lost; युयुधानः सात्यकिः ॥१॥ — Yuyudhana and Satyaki.
1.translation: In the fifty-eighth, Krishna took the five-hand\'s. I married Kalindi Mitravindha Satya Bhadra and Lakshmana Kalindi, who had undergone great austerities for her own benefit. After marrying his beloved wife, he returned to Indraprastha. Everyone saw them again in the house of Drupada even though they had appeared to be lost Yuyudhana and Satyaki.

2.word_for_word: प्राणा इन्द्रियाणि मुख्यं पञ्चवृत्तिं प्राणम् इव ॥ — The life air is the chief sense organ, and the five functions are the life force.; २-३ ॥ — 2-3 ॥
2.translation: The life air is the chief sense organ, and the five functions are the life force. 2-3 ॥

4.word_for_word: ज्येष्ठयोः प्रणामं कृत्वा समेनालिङ्गितः कनिष्ठाभ्याम् अभिवन्दितो बभूव ॥४॥ — Having bowed to the elder brothers he embraced them equally and was greeted by the younger brothers
4.translation: Having bowed to the elder brothers he embraced them equally and was greeted by the younger brothers

5.word_for_word: कृष्णा द्रौपदी । — Krishna Draupadi.; बहुभार्या सत्यपि निन्दारहिता पार्थैर् नवमचिरमूढा परिणीता ॥ — Although she had many wives, she was free from blasphemy and was soon married by the sons of Pṛthā.; ५-६ ॥ — 5-6 ॥
5.translation: Krishna Draupadi. Although she had many wives, she was free from blasphemy and was soon married by the sons of Pṛthā. 5-6 ॥

7.word_for_word: अतिहार्देन स्नेहेनार्द्रे सजले दृशौ यस्यास्तया परिष्वक्तः । — She embraced him with great affection, whose eyes were soaked with water.; तया परिपृष्टा बान्धवा यस्य सः ॥७॥ — She asked him whose relatives he was.
7.translation: She embraced him with great affection, whose eyes were soaked with water. She asked him whose relatives he was.

8.word_for_word: प्रेम्णा वैक्लव्यं तेन रुद्धः कण्ठो यस्याः क्लेशापाये आत्मनि दर्शनं यस्य तम् । — The one whose throat is choked by the disturbance of love is the one who sees himself in the end of his suffering.; भजतां क्लेशापायाय आत्मानं दर्शयतीति वा ॥८॥ — Or that He shows Himself to His devotees for the relief of their suffering.
8.translation: The one whose throat is choked by the disturbance of love is the one who sees himself in the end of his suffering. Or that He shows Himself to His devotees for the relief of their suffering.

9.word_for_word: ज्ञातीन् बन्धून नो\ऽस्मान् यदा भ्राताक्रूरः प्रेषितः ॥९॥ — When our cruel brother was sent to us our relatives and kinsmen
9.translation: When our cruel brother was sent to us our relatives and kinsmen

10.word_for_word: ज्ञातीनिति वचनात्प्राप्त मोहं वारयन्ती स्तौति । — She praises him for preventing the delusion she has gained from the words “relatives”.; न ते\ऽस्तोति । — He doesn\'t praise them.; तत्र हेतुः विश्वस्येति सुहृच् च आत्मा च तस्य हंसि नाशयसि ॥१०॥ — There is the cause of the universe, the friend and the self, and you destroy it in your swan.
10.translation: She praises him for preventing the delusion she has gained from the words “relatives”. He doesn\'t praise them. There is the cause of the universe, the friend and the self, and you destroy it in your swan.

11.word_for_word: कुमेधसां विषयासक्तचित्तानां दृष्टो\ऽसि ॥११॥ — Thou art seen by the foolish whose minds are attached to sensual pleasures.
11.translation: Thou art seen by the foolish whose minds are attached to sensual pleasures.

12.word_for_word: सुखम् अवसद् इति शेषः । — The rest is that he lived happily.; सुखम् अभ्यर्थित इति वा क्रिया-समाप्तिः ॥१२॥ — or the completion of the action, that is, happiness is requested.
12.translation: The rest is that he lived happily. or the completion of the action, that is, happiness is requested.

13-14.word_for_word: कालिन्दी-दर्शन-प्रसङ्गम् आह---एकदा इति । — He argues for the occasion of seeing Kalindi: Once.; अक्षयाः सायका ययोस् तौ तूणौ इषुधी ॥ — The arrows of these two quivers are inexhaustible.; १३-१५ ॥ — 13-15.
13-14.translation: He argues for the occasion of seeing Kalindi: Once. The arrows of these two quivers are inexhaustible. 13-15.

16-17.word_for_word: राज्ञ युधिष्ठिराय मेध्यान् कर्मार्हान्, बीभत्सुरर्जौनः ॥ — The terrible demon Arjuna offered sacrificial offerings to King Yudhiṣṭhira.; १६-१७ ॥ — 16-17.
16-17.translation: The terrible demon Arjuna offered sacrificial offerings to King Yudhiṣṭhira. 16-17.

21.word_for_word: अयं मां कामयेदित्याशङ्कायाम् आह । — When he suspected that he might desire me, he said; नान्यम् इति ॥ — Nothing else, it is.; २१-२२ ॥ — 21-22.
21.translation: When he suspected that he might desire me, he said Nothing else, it is. 21-22.

23.word_for_word: आदावेव तद्विद्वान् ॥२३॥ — He knew it in the beginning.
23.translation: He knew it in the beginning.

24.word_for_word: प्रसङ्गातसत्कालीनं चरित्रान्तरम् आह---यदैवेति । — He argues that the character change in the context is whenever.; पार्थैर् यदैव सन्दिष्टो विज्ञापितः श्री-कृष्णस्तदैव तेषां विश्वकर्मणा देवशिल्पिना नगर कारयामास ॥२४॥ — As soon as Lord Kṛṣṇa was instructed and informed by the sons of Arjuna, Visvakarma, the sculptor of the gods, built a city for them.
24.translation: He argues that the character change in the context is whenever. As soon as Lord Kṛṣṇa was instructed and informed by the sons of Arjuna, Visvakarma, the sculptor of the gods, built a city for them.

25-26.word_for_word: किं च, भगवान्निरतिशयैश्वर्यगुणवानप्यर्जुनस्य धनुरादिलाभाय सारथिरास खाण्डवं नामेद्रस्य वनम् ॥२५॥ — What is more, although endowed with unsurpassed opulence and virtues, the charioteer entered the forest of Indra named Khandava to obtain Arjuna's bow and other objects.; अक्षयावक्षयसायकौ ॥२६॥ — They are inexhaustible and inexhaustible.
25-26.translation: What is more, although endowed with unsurpassed opulence and virtues, the charioteer entered the forest of Indra named Khandava to obtain Arjuna's bow and other objects. They are inexhaustible and inexhaustible.

27.word_for_word: खाण्डवदाहकाद्वह्ने, सख्ये अर्जुनाय यस्मिन्न् इति सामान्यतो निर्देशः यस्याम् इत्य् अर्थः । — In the fire from the burning of the Khandava, in which the friend Arjuna is generally directed, means in whom.; जलस्थलयोर् दृशेर्दृष्टेभ्रमः । — The illusion of sight between water and land.; यद् वा, जले स्थलवत् दृक् दृष्टिर्यस्मिंस्तज्जलस्थलदृक् तस्मिन् भ्रम असीद् इति ॥ — In other words, one’s vision is like that of land in water, and one’s vision is like that of land in water.; २७-२८ ॥ — 27-28.
27.translation: In the fire from the burning of the Khandava, in which the friend Arjuna is generally directed, means in whom. The illusion of sight between water and land. In other words, one’s vision is like that of land in water, and one’s vision is like that of land in water. 27-28.

29.word_for_word: सुपुण्य ऋतुः ऋक्षं च यस्मिन् ॥२९॥ — The auspicious season in which the bear is present.
29.translation: The auspicious season in which the bear is present.

30.word_for_word: पञ्चमं मित्रविदाविवाहम् आह---विन्दाव् इति द्वाभ्याम् । — The fifth marriage of Mitravida is argued by two, Vindav.; आवन्त्याववन्त्याराजानौ ॥ — They were the kings of Avantya and Avantya.; ३०-३१ ॥ — 30-31.
30.translation: The fifth marriage of Mitravida is argued by two, Vindav. They were the kings of Avantya and Avantya. 30-31.

32.word_for_word: षष्ठम् आह । — The sixth is argued.; नग्नजिद् इति । — Nagnajid is the name.; कौशल्यो\ऽयोध्यापतिस्तस्य सत्या नाम कन्या\ऽभवदासीत् देवी कान्तिमती नाग्नजितीति पितृनाम्ना प्रसिद्ध त्य् अर्थः ॥३२॥ — Kaushalya the lord of Ayodhya had a daughter named Satya who was a goddess named Kantimati and was well known by her father's name Nagnajiti
32.translation: The sixth is argued. Nagnajid is the name. Kaushalya the lord of Ayodhya had a daughter named Satya who was a goddess named Kantimati and was well known by her father's name Nagnajiti

33.word_for_word: वीरस्य गन्धम् अपि न सहन्त इति तथा तान् खलान् दुर्वृत्तान् ॥३३॥ — They could not even tolerate the smell of a hero and so did those wicked and evil-doers.
33.translation: They could not even tolerate the smell of a hero and so did those wicked and evil-doers.

34.word_for_word: वृषान् जयति यस् तेन लभ्याम् ॥३४॥ — I shall be obtained by him who conquers the bulls.
34.translation: I shall be obtained by him who conquers the bulls.

35.word_for_word: प्रतिनन्दितस्तं प्रतिनन्दितवान् । — He greeted him back.; श्री-कृष्णेन वा स प्रतिनन्दितः ॥ — Or he was greeted by Lord Kṛṣṇa.; ३५-३९ ॥ — 35-39.
35.translation: He greeted him back. Or he was greeted by Lord Kṛṣṇa. 35-39.

40.word_for_word: हे नरेन्द्र । — O Narendra.; राजन्यबन्धोः क्षत्रियस्य । — of the royal bond of the Kshatriya.; शुल्कदा द्रव्यादिप्रदाः ॥४०॥ — They pay fees and give goods and other things.
40.translation: O Narendra. of the royal bond of the Kshatriya. They pay fees and give goods and other things.

41.word_for_word: गुणानामेकम् एव धाम स्थानं तथा-भूतस्य यस्य तवाङ्गे ॥ — The Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is situated in Your body, is the only abode of the modes of material nature.; ४१-४२ ॥ — 41-42.
41.translation: The Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is situated in Your body, is the only abode of the modes of material nature. 41-42.

43.word_for_word: दुर्दाता अशिक्षिताः । — Bad givers are uneducated.; दुरवग्रहा अपरायत्ताः । — They are difficult to grasp and are innocent.; कुतस्तदाह---एतैर् इति । — Where then does he say, by these?; भग्ना भङ्ग प्रापिताः ॥ — They were broken and broken.; ४३ — 43
43.translation: Bad givers are uneducated. They are difficult to grasp and are innocent. Where then does he say, by these? They were broken and broken. 43

44.word_for_word: यद्यदीमे गोवृषा निगृहीता दमिता नाथिता इति यावत् ॥४४॥ — If these cows and bulls are restrained, restrained and neglected, that is to say.
44.translation: If these cows and bulls are restrained, restrained and neglected, that is to say.

45.word_for_word: एतान्यो निगृह्णाति तस्य कन्येति समयः कृतस्तम् । — These others are restraining him, and the time has come for him to say that he is his daughter.; सप्तधा कृत्वेति बह्वीनां योषितां सम्पूर्ण एवाहं संभोगयोग्यः स्याम् इति सत्यां प्रत्यसापत्न्यप्रदर्शनार्थमात्मनः सप्तधा करणम् ॥ — He divided himself into seven parts to demonstrate his truthfulness to many women, saying, “I am complete and worthy of sexual intercourse.” Thus he divided himself into seven parts.; ४५-४९ ॥ — 45-49.
45.translation: These others are restraining him, and the time has come for him to say that he is his daughter. He divided himself into seven parts to demonstrate his truthfulness to many women, saying, “I am complete and worthy of sexual intercourse.” Thus he divided himself into seven parts. 45-49.

50.word_for_word: निष्कग्रीवाश् च ताः सुवाससश् च तासां युवतीनां च दासीनाम् ॥५०॥ — They were naked and dressed in fine clothes and they were young maidservants.
50.translation: They were naked and dressed in fine clothes and they were young maidservants.

51.word_for_word: नागान् नागेभ्यः शत-गुणान् नव---लक्षाणि । — Nine---millions of snakes, a hundred times as many as snakes.; रथाद्रथेभ्यः शत-गुणान्नकोटौः । — Two crores of food a hundred times more than chariots.; अश्वादश्वेभ्यः शत-गुणान्नवपद्मानि ॥ — Nine lotuses are one hundred times better than horses.; ५१-५२ ॥ — 51-52.
51.translation: Nine---millions of snakes, a hundred times as many as snakes. Two crores of food a hundred times more than chariots. Nine lotuses are one hundred times better than horses. 51-52.

53.word_for_word: यदुभिर् गोवृषैश् च भग्नवीर्या अपि सुदुर्मर्षा असहनशीला रुरुधुः ॥५३॥ — They were impatient and intolerant even though their prowess had been shattered by the Yadus and cows and bulls
53.translation: They were impatient and intolerant even though their prowess had been shattered by the Yadus and cows and bulls

54.word_for_word: अस्यतः क्षिपतः प्रयुजानानिति यावत् ॥५४-५५॥ — That is, they used it when they threw it away.54-5
54.translation: That is, they used it when they threw it away.54-5

56.word_for_word: सप्तमं विवाहम् आह---श्रुतकीर्तेर् इति । — The seventh marriage is said to be that of Shrutakirti.; श्रुतकीर्तिर्नाम या पितृष्वसा तस्याः सुतां भद्रां नाम कैकेयीं तद्देशजाम् ॥५६॥ — His paternal aunt named Śrutakirti gave birth to a daughter named Kaikeyi named Bhadra who was born in that country
56.translation: The seventh marriage is said to be that of Shrutakirti. His paternal aunt named Śrutakirti gave birth to a daughter named Kaikeyi named Bhadra who was born in that country

57.word_for_word: अष्टम विवाहम् आह । — The eighth marriage is called.; सुतां चेति । — and his daughter.; एक एव स श्री-कृष्णो लक्ष्मणां जहार ॥५७॥ — That alone Lord Krishna took away Lakshmana.
57.translation: The eighth marriage is called. and his daughter. That alone Lord Krishna took away Lakshmana.

58.word_for_word: तस्य निरोधोन्तःपुरं तस्मात् ॥ — Therefore the inner palace of the Lord is called Nirodho.; ५८ ॥ — 58 ॥; भैष्मी जांबवती भामा सत्या भद्रा च लक्ष्मणा । — Bhīṣmī, Jāmbavatī, Bhāmā, Satya, Bhadrā and Lakṣmaṇa.; कालिन्दी मित्रविन्दा चेत्यष्टौ पट्टमहास्त्रियः ॥ — There were eight great women named Kālindī and Mitravindha.
58.translation: Therefore the inner palace of the Lord is called Nirodho. 58 ॥ Bhīṣmī, Jāmbavatī, Bhāmā, Satya, Bhadrā and Lakṣmaṇa. There were eight great women named Kālindī and Mitravindha.
